## What a counter cannot see

**Two readings, both from the document.** SABER (arXiv:2608.27963) branches the
prefix at every "Wait" into a neutral and an adversarial probe and stops when
the two agree; it is one of the few in this family to report probe overhead
(3.8% of tokens) and wall-clock latency (48.8% shorter) separately from token
counts, though it never says whether its own compression ratios are gross or
net of that overhead, and Table 1 cannot be reconciled with Table 3 from the
paper alone. The abduction paper (arXiv:2609.01867) is not a stopping method:
it correlates reasoning-token count with human reaction time per item and
finds every one of eight models significant, which gives this topic an
external criterion for how long a problem should take — neither accuracy nor
an estimated lower bound — and a caution, since humans score below chance on
the items the models get wrong.

**DEER's entry was rewritten because its standing changed, not its mechanism.**
The old text carried the method's self-report (19.1–80.1% of tokens cut,
accuracy up 0.3–5.0%). Independent runs do not reproduce the accuracy gain:
SABER puts DEER at 66.7 overall against 67.8 for unmodified reasoning on
DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B while using 78.3% of the tokens. That is the same
self-report-versus-reproduction gap this archive has been recording elsewhere,
now visible inside a single entity's definition.

**Two entities changed shape rather than gaining detail.** Omni-MATH now has a
third role: the shared-budget rationing benchmarks use it for its difficulty
labels, not its mathematics. StrategyQA is still undefined by every source
that cites it, but its role is now legible — the non-mathematical control in
an archive that is otherwise almost entirely mathematics, with ReTraceQA's
warning attached, that on commonsense QA a correct answer arrives through a
flawed trace 14–24% of the time.

**Left deliberately undone.** The definition of *Overthinking* is not merely
behind at 52 sources against 80; one clause of it is wrong. It states that
mitigation methods report "30–70% token reductions at little or no accuracy
cost", which this archive's own external-reproduction readings contradict.
It cannot be re-queued: the refresh threshold is 2.0 and this entity sits at
1.54, and lowering the threshold ranks by ratio, so it would still not surface.
The targeted route is to clear its `definition` field so render asks for it
again with all 80 sources attached. That edit was not made — it needs a
decision from the archive's owner, since clearing discards a ruling most of
which is still right.

**Collection found nothing, twice, for different reasons.** The first run lost
every arXiv query to HTTP 429, including all five topic searches covering
2026-09-04 to 09-07, and skipped 38 curated picks that could not be resolved.
The retry half an hour later reached arXiv cleanly and still archived nothing
new: 786 collected, 730 rejected, 56 past the bar, all of them already held.
The archive is genuinely current on this topic — the newest papers it holds
are the two read today.

## Second session — draining the refresh queue

Twenty-five definitions revised in parallel by five Sonnet 5 agents, five
each, submitted through the queue validator like any other answer. That
clears everything the archive can ask for: 170 definitions remain stale but
sit below the 2.0 refresh threshold, so nothing re-queues them and lowering
that threshold is a separate decision, not a cleanup.

`max_refresh_tasks` was raised from 5 to 30 for one render so all twenty-five
could be taken at once, then restored. The pacing is deliberate — five per
render is what keeps a neglected archive drainable rather than unfaceable —
and it is back where it was.

**Two corrections found by the reviewers, both worth more than the revisions
that surfaced them.** The o1 and o1-mini entries had bled into each other: the
claim that seed data was gathered from o1's reasoning flow sat in o1-mini's
definition, when the Long CoT Collection paper names o1 alone as the teacher
and lists o1-mini only among its evaluated models. The reverse error was
there too — Mousetrap tests o1 directly, not only through o1-mini. Both are
now answered against their own sources. This is the failure mode the alias
rule exists for, arriving through prose instead of through an alias.

SuperGPQA's previous definition credited a provenance claim to
OptimalThinkingBench, which is no longer among the sources attached to that
entity. The claim was dropped rather than carried forward on trust.

**What the reviewers could not fix.** Several entries still say, correctly,
that no source describes the entity at all — NoThinking's mechanism is named
by four papers and explained by none; Dynasor is a baseline everyone compares
against and nobody defines. Those definitions record a gap rather than filling
it, which is the right answer and also a standing invitation: the papers that
would close them are not in the archive.

**Duplicate check, read-only.** `pipelines.duplicates` reports 766 candidates
and almost all are false: the rules match on suffix and near-string, so they
pair genuinely different years (AIME 2024 / 2025), releases
(LiveCodeBench v5 / v6) and even different models (DeepSeek-R1 / V3). The
shape of a real candidate is narrower — a singleton with no definition that is
a sloppier spelling of an established entity, such as `deepseek-3` or
`deepseek-8b`. Nothing was merged; concept merging is not what `dedupe` covers.
